summary: Blurs an image per pixel using luminance or greyscale values from a second input, with separate blur widths for black and white control values.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: catmull, gaussian, box, bartlette, sinc, hanning, or blackman kernel

key_params.name: widthchan
key_params.note: luminance, rgba channels, rgbaverage, or average blur driver

key_params.name: blackvalue
key_params.note: Input channel value mapped to black filter width

key_params.name: whitevalue
key_params.note: Input channel value mapped to white filter width

key_params.name: blackwidth
key_params.note: Blur width where the second input is black

key_params.name: whitewidth
key_params.note: Blur width where the second input is white

key_params.name: extend
key_params.note: hold, zero, repeat, or mirror blur sampling at edges

common_gotchas: A meaningful second input is essential; a flat driver produces a uniform blur.
Sinc can preserve detail but may introduce ringing artifacts.
Box is cheaper but visibly boxy compared with Gaussian or Catmull-Rom.
Large blackwidth or whitewidth values can be expensive on high-resolution textures.
The official token is bartlette, preserving the docs spelling.
key_concepts: Uses a second input luminance or channel image to vary blur width per pixel.
Black and white filter widths define blur amounts at the two ends of the driving channel.
Kernel type changes sharpness, ringing, cost, and edge behavior.
Extend controls how samples outside the source image are treated during blur.
The operator supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.
